result.title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Induce Local Geometry for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting
result.summary: Catastrophic forgetting remains a challenge in supervised continual learning, as adapting to new tasks causes representation drift and loss of previously learned information. This raises the question of which representational changes should be constrained while preserving plasticity. We therefore introduce Sparse Autoencoder Geometric Anchoring (SAGA), which converts a Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) trained at each task boundary into local, low-rank constraints on representation drift. Replay examples specify where the constraints apply, while leading right singular directions of the encoder Jacobian specify which changes are penalized. The resulting geometry is input dependent and can be retained without keeping the SAE for subsequent tasks' training. We establish its local relation to latent code matching, define its spectral truncation error, and derive a conditional bound on frozen-readout drift. With replay and snapshot history, the method achieves the highest mean Class-IL accuracy and lowest mean forgetting among the evaluated ER, DER++, ER-ACE, and SGD baselines on three pretrained ViT-B/16 benchmarks, with accuracy gains of 12.15, 4.79, and 3.22 percentage points over the strongest conventional baseline on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and ImageNet-R, respectively. From scratch results are more mixed, while rank ablations and geometry controls show that SAE-induced low-rank geometry offers useful stability-plasticity trade-offs.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SAGA，在持续学习的任务边界上训练稀疏自编码器，把表征漂移约束转化为输入依赖的低秩几何锚定：由回放样本指定约束位置，由编码器 Jacobian 的主右奇异方向指定被惩罚的变化，并在三个预训练 ViT-B/16 基准上评测稳定性—可塑性权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用 SAE 与 Jacobian 主奇异方向刻画局部表征几何」的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的漂移诊断、以及判断哪些内部方向承载任务必要视觉信息提供可供核查的方法线索，但原文是图像分类的持续学习，未涉及推理或多模态生成。
